title: THE IDOLS YOU HAVE TO HIDE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob answered Laban, 'I was afraid, because I thought you would take your daughters away from me by force. But if you find anyone who has your gods, that person shall not live. In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself whether there is anything of yours here with me; and if so, take it.' Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the gods. So Laban went into Jacob's tent and into Leah's tent and into the tent of the two female servants, but he found nothing. After he came out of Leah's tent, he entered Rachel's tent. Now Rachel had taken the household gods and put them inside her camel's saddle and was sitting on them. Laban searched through everything in the tent but found nothing. Rachel said to her father, 'Don't be angry, my lord that I cannot stand up in your presence; I'm having my period.' So he searched but could not find the household gods." - Gen 31:31-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The scene that follows is almost comical, if it were not so revealing. Laban rummages through tent after tent, hunting for his precious "gods." All the while, Rachel is sitting on them — she has hidden the idols in her camel's saddle and stays seated with an excuse so her father will not make her rise. The great "gods" of Laban's household are stuffed under a young woman and cannot even reveal their own hiding place.

What a picture of the emptiness of idols. Here is a god small enough to steal, light enough to sit on, and helpless to defend itself. It has to be hidden, protected, and carried about by people. A god like that can do nothing for anyone.

The contrast with the living God could not be sharper. The true God is not carried by us — He carries us. He is not hidden by us — He sees all. He is not protected by us — He protects His own.

And yet, we should be honest: idols still linger, even among believers. Rachel was part of the covenant family, yet she clung to these little gods. What might we be secretly "sitting on" — a hidden habit, a treasured possession, a comfort we cannot let go? Idols must eventually be brought into the open and buried (Gen 35:4). Ask God to remove whatever quietly competes for the throne of your heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What might I be secretly "sitting on" — a hidden idol I cannot let go?
2. Do I trust the living God who carries me, not a god I must carry?
3. What competes for the throne of my heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, search my heart and expose any hidden idol I am clinging to. You are the living God who carries me; help me to bury every rival and to trust You alone. Amen.
